safety_lead_time.comparison_action: reduce SAP safety lead time from 2.5 days to 0.83 days

narrative: Material PL2__M0DC4D1D exhibits high-volume, near-continuous demand averaging 352,405 units/day with a moderate CV of 0.254 and no statistically significant trend across the 214-day observation window. Lead times are short on average (0.47 days) but exhibit high relative variability (CV 1.03), with sporadic spikes to 2.76 days driving 93.6% of the safety buffer requirement. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with reorder point 629,692 and order quantity 84,737 maintains the 95% service level while reducing holding costs by approximately $47,700/year compared to the current SAP configuration.
warnings: Lead time CV > 1.0 (moderately unstable); monitor for further deterioration
SAP safety lead time of 2.5 days exceeds data-derived recommendation of 0.83 days — consider downward revision

research_insights.selection_rationale: High, near-daily demand volume with a stable mean and moderate CV makes the EOQ-based (r,Q) policy optimal. The policy is straightforward to configure in SAP as a reorder-point trigger with a fixed lot size, and the ordering cost is sufficiently low relative to holding costs that frequent small replenishments are economically justified.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage utilization is approximately 11.6% (376,254 / 2,879,354 units), leaving ample headroom. The capacity constraint does not bind and does not reduce service level or inflate costs.
